query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Browse a Bitbucket repository directory tree and retrieve selected repository file contents.
query_ground_truth.intent: Retrieve the hierarchical list of files and folders within a Bitbucket repository directory.

results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Read repository metadata using GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY (confirm default branch/ref to browse).
[Required] [Step]: List top-level contents using GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT (get immediate folders/files at root).
[Optional (if you need a complete inventory)] [Step]: Fetch a full hierarchy using GITHUB_GET_A_TREE (recursive) and summarize paths client-side.
[Optional (if exploring by keyword)] [Step]: Locate relevant areas using GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE (find matching files), then inspect surrounding directories using GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.
[Optional (if documentation is in a wiki)] [Next Step]: Browse docs structure using DEEPWIKI_MCP_READ_WIKI_STRUCTURE, then open pages using DEEPWIKI_MCP_READ_WIKI_CONTENTS.
[Optional (if directory listings are too fragmented/slow)] [Fallback]: Prefer a single recursive snapshot using GITHUB_GET_A_TREE (reduce repeated GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT calls).
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT] Large root listings can be inefficient to traverse via repeated per-folder calls; switch to GITHUB_GET_A_TREE for breadth.
[GITHUB_GET_A_TREE] Recursive output is a flat list of paths requiring client-side filtering/grouping to rebuild a directory view.
[GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE] Results are match-driven (not a full inventory); use it to jump to likely locations, then confirm structure via GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.

GITHUB_GET_A_TREE.description: Browse and list all files/directories in a GitHub repository. Efficiently retrieves the complete repository structure in a single API call when used with recursive mode. Perfect for analyzing codebase structure, finding specific files, or getting an overview of repository contents without cloning.

repo.description: Repository name without owner or .git extension (e.g., for github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes, repo is 'kubernetes').

owner.description: Repository owner username or organization name (e.g., for github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes, owner is 'kubernetes').

tree_sha.description: Branch name (e.g., 'main', 'master'), tag name (e.g., 'v1.0.0'), commit SHA, or tree SHA. Directory paths are NOT supported - use a branch/tag to get the full tree, then extract the directory's SHA from results.

recursive.description: Set to True (or '1'/'true') to fetch the ENTIRE repository file tree recursively (all files and directories in one call). Set to False or leave empty to fetch only the top-level files/folders. For browsing or analyzing the full repository structure, use recursive=True.

GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.description: Retrieves a file's Base64 encoded content or lists a directory's contents from a GitHub repository.

ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.

path.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.

repo.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: Required. The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive. Can also accept full repository path in format 'owner/repo' - the repo part will be extracted automatically.

GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE.description: Searches code file contents and paths on the default branch of GitHub repositories using a query string; searches only files under 384KB, returns max 1000 results by best match, and is optimized for precision.

q.description: Code search query, including keywords and qualifiers (e.g., `language:python`, `user:octocat`, `repo:owner/repo`). For full syntax and qualifiers, see GitHub docs: [Constructing a search query](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#constructing-a-search-query) and [code search qualifiers](https://docs.github.com/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-code).

page.description: Page number for results. For pagination details, see GitHub docs: [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

sort.description: DEPRECATED. Valid: 'indexed' (sorts by last indexed time) or 'updated' (sorts by last updated time). If unspecified, results sorted by best match. Docs: [ranking search results](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

order.description: DEPRECATED. Order ('asc' or 'desc') for results; effective only if `sort` is specified. Docs: [ranking search results](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

per_page.description: Results per page (max 100). For pagination details, see GitHub docs: [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).
